reason: No prior evidence is cited for any of the key premises. The claims about copper's thermal conductivity relative to the HEA, the mechanical effect of coherent nanoprecipitates, the feasibility of the synthesis route, and the predicted property retention are all presented without supporting references.
premises: Copper precipitates have higher intrinsic thermal conductivity than the HEA matrix
Nanoscale, coherently bonded precipitates do not create large-scale defects or interfaces that compromise mechanical integrity
~5 vol% Cu can be uniformly dispersed as nanoscale precipitates via the proposed powder metallurgy + HIP + annealing route
The precipitates form continuous conductive pathways that lower thermal resistance
The modified alloy retains yield strength and ductility comparable to the untreated HEA at ~700°C under cyclic loading
